title: PipeReader-Based JSON Parsing Changes
description: Understand the changes to PipeReader-based JSON parsing in System.Text.Json in .NET 10 and adapt your high-performance streaming code.

data.text: System.Text.Json supports high-performance deserialization from a PipeReader, allowing you to parse JSON directly from a stream without buffering the entire payload in memory. This is critical for high-throughput APIs processing large payloads or reading from network streams.

In .NET 10, the behavior of PipeReader-based deserialization changed in two important ways. First, the deserializer now respects the JsonSerializerOptions.PropertyNameCaseInsensitive setting when matching JSON property names during PipeReader reads. Second, the handling of trailing data after a complete JSON object now differs — previously ignored trailing bytes are now surfaced as a JsonException.

data.title: Breaking Change: Trailing Data Now Throws
data.text: If your PipeReader-based parsing code previously silently accepted trailing bytes after a complete JSON payload, it will now throw a JsonException. You must explicitly consume or discard trailing data before deserializing.

The recommended pattern is to read from the PipeReader until the JSON payload is complete, then deserialize. If you expect multiple JSON objects in a single stream (newline-delimited JSON), read and deserialize each object separately.

data.title: Correct PipeReader deserialization in .NET 10
data.content: Read a complete JSON payload from a PipeReader and deserialize it

data.text: For newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) streams, use JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsyncEnumerable with a PipeReader. The .NET 10 implementation correctly advances the reader past each object, so trailing whitespace or newlines between objects no longer cause failures.

data.title: Deserialize multiple objects from a stream
data.content: Use DeserializeAsyncEnumerable with a stream in .NET 10

data.title: Migration Steps
items: Audit all PipeReader-based deserialization code for trailing data assumptions.
Ensure the reader is advanced past consumed bytes after each parse attempt.
Add explicit handling for incomplete JSON at the end of the stream.

data.title: Summary
points: Trailing data after a complete JSON object now throws in .NET 10.
Use DeserializeAsyncEnumerable for newline-delimited JSON streams.
Always advance the PipeReader past consumed bytes to avoid re-reading.
Set PropertyNameCaseInsensitive explicitly for predictable behavior.
data.takeaway: The PipeReader changes in .NET 10 make JSON streaming more strict and predictable, which catches bugs early but requires updating existing high-performance deserialization code.
